source.title: Some open problems in the context of skew PBW extensions and semi-graded rings

accepted.question_text: Let B = ⊕_{n≥0} B_n be a semi-graded ring satisfying the conditions that B is left noetherian, B_0 is left noetherian, each B_n is a finitely generated left B_0-module, and B_0 is contained in the center Z(B). Assuming also that B satisfies the χ_1 condition, does the semi-graded analogue of the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem hold, namely is there an equivalence of categories qgr − B ≃ qgr − Γ(π(B))_{≥0}?

evidence.quote: • Investigate the Serre-Artin-Zhang-Verevkin theorem for semi-graded rings.

The solution of Problem 1 is as follows. Theorem 1.24. Let B be a SG ring that satisfies (C1)-(C4) and assume that B satisfies the condition X1, then there exists an equivalence of categories qgr − B ≃ qgr − Γ(π(B))≥0. (1.10)

accepted.question_text: If A is a bijective skew PBW extension over an Ore domain, can one prove a Gelfand-Kirillov-type description of its total ring of fractions, and in particular does one have an isomorphism between the total ring of fractions of the center and the center of the total ring of fractions, Q(Z(A)) ≅ Z(Q(A))?
accepted.context_brief: Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for skew PBW extensions

evidence.quote: • Study the Gelfand-Kirillov conjecture for bijective skew P BW extensions over Ore domains. More-over, investigate for them the isomorphism Q(Z(A)) ∼= Z(Q(A)).
In [2] was proved the following partial solution of Problem 2.

accepted.question_text: Let A := K[x_1, . . . , x_n; σ], where K is a field, σ is an automorphism of K of finite order, the variables x_i commute with one another, and x_i r = σ(r) x_i for every r ∈ K and 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n. Can one give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for this ring and, moreover, produce an explicit algorithm that computes a basis for any given finitely generated projective A-module?
accepted.context_brief: Constructive Quillen-Suslin for skew polynomial rings

evidence.quote: • Give a matrix-constructive proof of the Quillen-Suslin theorem for A := K[x1, . . . , xn; σ]. Include an algorithm that computes a basis of a given finitely generated projective A-module.

In [21] was solved the previous problem for the case of only one variable, in this particular situation weaker hypotheses can be set, namely, K is a division ring, σ is not necessarily of finite order and a non trivial σ-derivation δ of K can be added.

accepted.question_text: If B is a left semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra (SAS) with finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension, must B be a left noetherian domain?

evidence.quote: • Is any SAS algebra with finite GKdim a left noetherian domain?

Remark 4.15. From the general homological properties of skew P BW extensions we know that if R is a noetherian domain, then A is a noetherian domain ([38]). This agrees with the question of Problem 4.

accepted.question_text: Let B be a semi-graded Artin-Schelter regular algebra over a field K of characteristic 0, and assume that B is left and right noetherian, generated in degree 1, and has global dimension 3. Must B be cancellative; that is, whenever B[t] is isomorphic to C[t] as K-algebras for some K-algebra C, does it follow that B is isomorphic to C?

evidence.quote: • Let B be a SAS algebra over a field K with char(K) = 0. Assume that B is noetherian (left and right), generated in degree 1 and gld(B) = 3. Is B cancellative?

Observe that if in the previous theorem we could remove the condition not P I, then the classical commutative ZCP problem would be solved for n = 3. With this, we can formulate our last problem in the next subsection.

accepted.question_text: For an Artin-Schelter regular algebra A, must A always be noetherian?

evidence.quote: (iii) Artin-Schelter open problems: In [9] were formulated the following problems: 1. Any AS algebra is noetherian?

There are some advances with respect to the previous open problems: Both questions above have positive answer for any AS algebra of dimension ≤ 3. In addition, the same is true for all known concrete examples of AS algebras of higher dimension.

accepted.question_text: For an Artin-Schelter regular algebra A, must A always be a domain?

evidence.quote: (iii) Artin-Schelter open problems: In [9] were formulated the following problems: 2. Any AS algebra is a domain?

There are some advances with respect to the previous open problems: Both questions above have positive answer for any AS algebra of dimension ≤ 3. In addition, the same is true for all known concrete examples of AS algebras of higher dimension. If A is AS noetherian and its dimension is ≤ 4, then A is a domain.
